purpose: Canonical vocabulary for the Tim Dooley / Potato of Life framework. Terms are definitions within the project unless explicitly marked otherwise.

entries.definition: The central seed/plant metaphor: ordinary, buried, rooted, growing and capable of becoming life-giving.
The evolving project mythology/worldview organized around the Potato of Life, Source, Father, Son, Axis, Tree, Door, Plane and transformation from strife toward life.
The enclosing or ordering structure through which reality can be represented; a foundational project concept above the ordinary field of objects.
Central line of orientation joining the symbolic levels.
The project's north-oriented central axis: direction, alignment, summit and orientation.
A symbolic beyond-North pole representing ultimate orientation.
Symbolic threshold associated with northern orientation and entry/exit through the axial field.
Symbolic seat of axial/northern authority.
Originating/generative archetype in the project mythology.
The Father understood through the project's heaven/sourceward orientation.
Symbolic dwelling/chamber of the Father; associated in the project's anatomical metaphor with the thalamus.
Originating depth/principle from which the architecture proceeds.
Upper/sourceward domain or orientation.
Vertical sequence of levels representing development, ascent, descent and connection.
Living upward-growing network of root, trunk, branches and fruit.
Complementary tree of conflict, fear, fragmentation, memory and struggle.
Grounding, ancestry, memory and hidden nourishment.
The produced consequence of growth that can nourish others.
Potential life contained within an apparently ordinary or dormant form.
Buried, obscured, materially dense starting condition.
Symbolic field of accumulated mud, confusion, fear and entanglement.
Symbolic summit and upward field of perspective/orientation.
Threshold/interface between domains; central symbol of passage and manifestation.
Relational Son/Vessel/threshold archetype positioned between Father/source and lived plane.
A carrier or container through which something from one domain can become present in another.
The lived interface or field in which dwellers encounter reality and one another.
A being/community occupying or relating to a symbolic plane or structure.
Symbolic position within unresolved mud; not a demographic or moral classification.
Symbolic position emphasizing ancestry, memory and grounding.
Symbolic position emphasizing living networks, branches and growth.
Symbolic position emphasizing levels and movement between them.
Symbolic position emphasizing alignment with the central axis.
Symbolic position within ordinary lived/social reality.
Symbolic threshold position emphasizing interface and translation.
Symbolic sourceward/heavenward orientation.
Illumination expressed through the Potato metaphor: light found within or emerging through ordinary life.
Archetype of creativity, love, light-seeking, sprouting, expansion and forward/upward movement.
Archetype of memory, meticulousness, fear, rooting, contraction and backward/downward movement.
Pattern of repeated movement through levels, widening below and narrowing above in the project's image.
Reorientation: changing direction from a destructive or disoriented trajectory toward a life-giving one.
Movement from buried/rooted conditions toward emergence and light.
Movement downward into roots, mud, memory or depth; potentially necessary for transformation.
Movement upward toward perspective, mountain, North and sourceward orientation.
Conflict, fear, fragmentation, disconnection and the conditions requiring transformation.
Growth, connection, love, creativity, cultivation and fruitfulness.
The transformation of destructive/warrior energy into cultivation, repair and creation.
A core transformation metaphor: force is redirected from destruction toward cultivation.
Comparative Christian-derived threshold image used for the Door: passage is concentrated and relational rather than infinitely diffuse.
A project comparative link to Davidic/root imagery in Jewish and Christian traditions.
Norse world-tree motif used comparatively for tree/axis/world-structure parallels.
Project language for a symbolic death/transformation of the Son within a memetic/mythic framework; not a claim about a historical event beyond documented history.
Project dimensional metaphor for extreme line/depth constraint or descent.
Project dimensional metaphor for surface/form/order.
Project dimensional metaphor for bounded material spatial reality.
Project metaphor for the time-bearing social/dweller plane.
Project metaphor for the threshold/interface associated with Son and pineal symbolism.
Project-symbolic motif for prolonged development, mastery or accumulated practice; not a scientific threshold.
Recurring project image of bounded structure, enclosure and dimensional order.
Project symbolic compound joining lunar/reflective imagery to the cube/enclosure motif.
Project symbolic medium of embodied life, ancestry, sacrifice and continuity; interpretation varies by context.
Project synthesis/metaphor for transformative embodied substance linking blood, alchemy and life.
Project metaphor for an actor who cultivates, harvests or manages souls/inner development; symbolic and not a claim about actual supernatural farming.
Project image of lower/supporting position beneath a higher authority or axis.
Connection structure that allows separated domains, people or levels to meet.
The process of bringing an individual, system or relationship back into alignment.

The user's broader policy/geopolitical framework for a connected northern-European economic, strategic and institutional network; maintained as a separate empirical/policy layer from Potatoism symbolism.
Project metaphor for stored value/resources/relationships accumulated through the Potato system.
A method of viewing ordinary objects and systems by repeatedly following their relationships until wider structures appear.
Start with something ordinary and keep following its relationships rather than stopping at the label.

classification_rule: Terms may belong to several families. The lexicon is deliberately graphable rather than a flat dictionary.
epistemic_rule: Project-defined terms are not external facts; historical names and comparative concepts must retain their own evidence status.
